reports.title: TEN, LTD. REPORTS RECORD PROFITS FOR THE NINE MONTHS AND THIRD QUARTER OF 2026

lines: The Company’s 9.25% Series E Preferred Shares become redeemable at the election of the Company on May 28, 2027, and the Company currently expects that it may elect to redeem, all or a portion of, such Series E Preferred Shares on the above stated date.

desk.headline: Revenue up 61% to $299.6m and EPS $5.57 incl. ship-sale gains, record profit; no formal guidance

numbers.eps_basis: diluted GAAP (includes $56.2m gain on ship sales)

results: Revenue rose 61% to $299.6m as tanker rates stayed strong; average earnings per ship rose 59% to $48,615 a day.
Profit was $174.5m, or $5.57 a share, including a $56.2m gain from selling three ships; analysts' $2.44 estimate likely excludes such gains.
Cash stood at $533.5m at the end of September; bank debt was $2.0bn.
A $150m buyback was approved in October and the first 2027 dividend was doubled to $1.00 a share.
Considering a second share listing in Singapore; no decision yet.

guidance.summary: TEN gives no formal earnings guidance; it points to $3.6bn of contracted future revenue.

points: Management said the company is adapting to a new, disrupted market and is signing long charters at high rates.
About 41% of the fleet has spot or profit-share exposure; each $1,000 a day move in spot rates changes yearly EPS by about $0.15.
A special dividend may come with the July payment, and the Series E preferred shares are expected to be redeemed in May 2027.
The company keeps avoiding the Strait of Hormuz; it named cost inflation and dearer new ships as risks.
